messages.subject: Aligning Maximum Data Values
parts:
I want to align the peaks of datasets in the following manner. 

cheeseb4<-structure(list(Type = structure(c(3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 
3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 2L, 
2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L), .Label = c("Camembert", 
"Cheddar", "Stilton"), class = "factor"), Day = c(0L, 1L, 2L, 
3L, 4L, 5L, 6L, 7L, 8L, 9L, 10L, 0L, 1L, 2L, 3L, 4L, 5L, 6L, 
7L, 8L, 9L, 10L, 0L, 1L, 2L, 3L, 4L, 5L, 6L, 7L, 8L, 9L, 10L), 
    Stinkiness = c(0L, 0L, 2L, 3L, 25L, 15L, 3L, 2L, 1L, 0L, 
    0L, 2L, 15L, 35L, 14L, 5L, 2L, 1L, 0L, 0L, 0L, 0L, 0L, 0L, 
    0L, 0L, 1L, 2L, 3L, 20L, 15L, 5L, 0L)), .Names = c("Type", 
"Day", "Stinkiness"), class = "data.frame", row.names = c(NA, 
-33L))

ggplot(data=cheeseb4, aes(x=Day, y=Stinkiness, colour=Type))+geom_line()

cheeseafter<-structure(list(Type = structure(c(3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 
3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 
1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 
2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L), .Label = c("Camembert", 
"Cheddar", "Stilton"), class = "factor"), Day = c(0L, 1L, 2L, 
3L, 4L, 5L, 6L, 7L, 8L, 9L, 10L, 11L, 12L, 13L, 14L, 15L, 0L, 
1L, 2L, 3L, 4L, 5L, 6L, 7L, 8L, 9L, 10L, 11L, 12L, 13L, 14L, 
15L, 0L, 1L, 2L, 3L, 4L, 5L, 6L, 7L, 8L, 9L, 10L, 11L, 12L, 13L, 
14L, 15L), Stinkiness = c(NA, NA, NA, 0L, 0L, 2L, 3L, 25L, 15L, 
3L, 2L, 1L, 0L, 0L, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, 2L, 15L, 35L, 
14L, 5L, 2L, 1L, 0L, 0L, 0L, 0L, 0L, 0L, 0L, 0L, 1L, 2L, 3L, 
20L, 15L, 5L, 0L, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA)), .Names = c("Type", "Day", 
"Stinkiness"), class = "data.frame", row.names = c(NA, -48L))

ggplot(data=cheeseafter, aes(x=Day, y=Stinkiness, colour=Type))+geom_line()

I thought about using ddply to define the maximum for each type of cheese and then using that as a reference for aligning the data.
ddply(cheeseb4, .(Type), function(x) transform(x, max=x$Stinkiness == max(x$Stinkiness)))

But, I have no idea how to slide the data to end up with what I have in cheeseafter. 

Anyone know of a way? Barking up the wrong mailing list?

Brandon

messages.author: 3a775dfa0a96bf95
messages.subject: Re: Aligning Maximum Data Values
parts:
Maybe something like this:

aligned <-  ddply(cheeseb4,'Type',transform, Day = Day  - which.max(Stinkiness))
ggplot(data=aligned, aes(x=Day, y=Stinkiness, colour=Type))+geom_line()
 
Of course, which.max is a pretty crude way of aligning, but for data with a clear single peak, I guess it's good enough....

            -s
